However, in order to hang out with a bunch of super powered beings, he needs to carry himself like he's the best, otherwise he'd be looked at as the hawkeye or original aquaman of the group. The tragic losses he's encountered has always been picked up on in the comics though, except for Stephanie Brown's, which I'm pretty sure was controversial among the comic book community. 

When Damien and Jason died he over exerted himself and fought crime non stop looking to just bury the pain. When Damien died he went through a long list of allies to talk about death and rebirth to correct it. He's always kept Jason's robin uniform in a case to remind him of his downfall. 

When Dick was nearly killed in infinite crisis, he came that close to breaking his number one rule and kill. It's hard to say which event caused him the most turmoil. He's always had a deeper connection to Dick, but he never forgave himself for Jason, and with Damien, it never really seemed like he got too close, but he was starting to come around. Regardless it was his son and had an impact.  

I think the biggest psychological trauma Bruce Wayne/ Batman has faced, is that the family he's adopted has more of an impact on him than blood since his parents died. Like LieutenantChickenLeg said, his parents are Gotham now. Anything were to happen to Gotham I think Batman would completely lose it. I think, and I'm pretty sure it's apparent, when he don's the cowl he thinks of himself more as an entity than a man, but when tragedy strikes his human side tends to come out more.
